Repeated-measures COVSTATIS

Source: R/covstatis_rm.R
covstatis_rm.Rd

Estimate the common covariance geometry and the covariance patterns that separate conditions in a balanced, one-factor repeated-measures design.

Usage

covstatis_rm(
  data,
  subject,
  condition,
  ncomp = 2L,
  ncomp_condition = NULL,
  norm_method = c("none", "frobenius", "mfa"),
  dcenter = FALSE,
  weights = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'covstatis_rm'
project_subjects(x, new_data, subject, condition, ...)

Arguments

data

List of covariance matrices, one per subject-condition cell. All matrices must be finite, symmetric, and describe the same variables in the same order. Supply consistent variable names throughout or use positional matching throughout. Positive semidefiniteness is assumed.

subject, condition

Vectors identifying the subject and condition of each matrix, in input order. Each subject must have one matrix per condition. Fitting requires at least two subjects and two conditions. Observed factor levels specify condition order. Other labels use order of first appearance.

ncomp

Maximum number of common variable axes to retain.

ncomp_condition

Maximum number of condition axes to retain. The default keeps all numerically supported axes, up to one fewer than the number of conditions.

norm_method

Per-cell scaling. The default, "none", preserves covariance magnitude. "frobenius" divides each matrix by its Frobenius norm and "mfa" divides by its largest eigenvalue.

dcenter

Apply Gower double centering to each cell before scaling. The default, FALSE, preserves covariance along the all-ones direction.

weights

Optional vector of nonnegative finite variable weights, with at least one positive entry. Unnamed weights follow matrix order. Named weights are matched to variable names. Each covariance entry (i, j) is multiplied by sqrt(w[i] * w[j]) before double centering and normalization. The fitted model stores the weights and applies them to raw projection matrices in the training variable order. The default gives unit weights.

x

A fitted `covstatis_rm` model.

new_data

Covariance matrices for one or more new subjects, with all training conditions observed once per subject. Supply `subject` and `condition` as for the training data.

...

Reserved for methods.

Value

A covstatis_rm list with the following fields:

  • common is the fitted COVSTATIS object on subject means.

  • weights contains the variable weights used for raw cells at fit and projection.

  • condition_effects contains one signed mean deviation matrix per condition.

  • condition_maps contains the retained Frobenius-orthonormal loading matrices.

  • condition_scores gives condition centroids on the retained axes.

  • paired_scores gives subject, condition, and component scores in input order.

  • explained gives the fraction of total condition-effect energy on each retained axis. sums_of_squares partitions total variation about the equal-cell grand mean into subject, condition, and residual terms. The residual includes subject-by-condition variation and estimation error.

A zero condition effect yields an empty list of maps and zero score columns. project_subjects() applies the fitted maps to complete panels of new subjects.

For `project_subjects()`, a list with `paired_scores` in input order and `common_scores`, one partial variable map per new subject.

Details

The common map is an ordinary covstatis() fit on each subject's average preprocessed covariance, with no further preprocessing. Variable weights apply to every cell in both analyses. The estimated STATIS table weights apply only to the common map.

For the condition analysis, subtract each subject's mean matrix from their cells, then average these paired deviations across subjects with equal weights. Decompose the resulting condition means using the Frobenius inner product. For each unit-norm loading matrix, the cell score is its inner product with that cell's paired deviation. Component signs are arbitrary. A tied set of components identifies a subspace up to rotation.

For two conditions, subtract the first fitted condition effect from the second to obtain the mean paired difference in the preprocessed units. Eigenvectors of this signed difference give variable combinations along which projected variance increased or decreased.

References

Madssen TS et al. (2021). Repeated measures ASCA+ for analysis of longitudinal intervention studies with multivariate outcome data. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009585 .

See also

covstatis(), design_mfa()

Examples

subject <- rep(c("s1", "s2", "s3"), each = 2)
condition <- rep(c("rest", "task"), 3)
cells <- lapply(seq_along(subject), function(i) {
  S <- diag(c(5 + match(subject[i], unique(subject)), 2, 2))
  S[2, 3] <- S[3, 2] <- if (condition[i] == "task") 0.5 else 0
  S
})
fit <- covstatis_rm(cells, subject, condition)
fit$common$roi_scores
#>          [,1]    [,2]
#> Obs_1 2.66117 0.00000
#> Obs_2 0.00000 1.06066
#> Obs_3 0.00000 1.06066
fit$paired_scores
#>   subject condition Component_1
#> 1      s1      rest  -0.3535534
#> 2      s1      task   0.3535534
#> 3      s2      rest  -0.3535534
#> 4      s2      task   0.3535534
#> 5      s3      rest  -0.3535534
#> 6      s3      task   0.3535534
delta <- fit$condition_effects$task - fit$condition_effects$rest
eigen(delta, symmetric = TRUE)$values
#> [1]  0.5  0.0 -0.5
